audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read a blanket 'Skill' while content win[0] is 'Ziggs' and win[1..6] are 'Xerath', matching the packet levelChart exactly. The full layer answered 'who wins Level 1' differently from the content layer on all seven rows.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range on a 6s cooldown at rank 1 and bounces past its landing point; Xerath's uncharged Q is 750. Level 1 genuinely belongs to Ziggs. From level 2 Xerath's W (1000) and then E (1050) outreach every Ziggs spell except the ult, and Ziggs has no mobility beyond a 20s Satchel Charge.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side to Ziggs with a rewritten why; phases[1..6].side to Xerath. Content layer already held these verdicts.

audit.why: Lost Chapter, level 6, Luden's and the late artillery-mirror spikes are all accurate, and spikes[1] correctly contrasts a channelled multi-shot R against Ziggs' single Mega Inferno Bomb (120/95/70s).

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Satchel Charge's knockback interrupts Rite of the Arcane. Xerath's R is flagged 'channel — interruptible: any CC cancels it' and Satchel Charge is flagged knockup at 1000 range — inside your own W range.
audit.why: This is the one thing Ziggs can do to a channelling Xerath, and it is the reason his Satchel cooldown is the green light for your ult, not just for your step-ups. The page treated Satchel purely as his escape.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns with Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12s, alongside the fact that Hexplosive Minefield (flat 16s) only slows and cannot break the channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Satchel Charge 20s/12s and Hexplosive Minefield's flat 16s.

audit.why: The brief's missingInteractions entry claims Satchel Charge 'bypasses stacking resistances' from a percentHealth flag, but Riot's own description of Satchel Charge says only magic damage plus a knock-away — no percent-health component. Per the flag-versus-description rule I trusted the description. Ziggs is entirely magic damage, so magic resist is in fact the correct answer against him.
audit.corrected: No edit written on that basis; flagged in notes so the flag can be corrected upstream.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2). dontsFull[2].d also referenced 'the dash', which Ziggs does not have. dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d were name-swap templates.
audit.why: Bodies contradicted their titles and named a mechanic absent from Ziggs' kit.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten to their titles from Ziggs' ranges, costs and cooldowns.

edits.before: Q from fog-of-war range on his every last-hit — level 1 Xerath is the longest gun in the lane. Mana is the only governor.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 and bounces past you before your W exists — soak XP, dodge the bounce, and wait for level 2.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Shocking Orb for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and 12s maxed — its knockback interrupts Rite of the Arcane, so never open the channel while it is up. - Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s and only slows; it cannot break the channel.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range on a 6s cooldown at rank 1 — after your Q lands his dodge is sideways, so put the 1000-range W there.

edits.before: Ziggs whiffs Satchel Charge and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Your Q costs 80 mana at rank 1; his Bouncing Bomb costs 50.

edits.before: That is Ziggs’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Inside 850 his Q bounces and his Short Fuse auto both land while you cast.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Past river he Satchels himself clear and his 5000-range Mega Inferno Bomb still reaches you — you gain nothing and hand him the map.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by mining your feet, knocking you out of the channel with Satchel, and closing from 5000 range.

notes: content win[0..6] already held Ziggs/Xerath x6 and match the packet exactly, so the full-layer side flips are unpaired by design — before==after win[N] edits would be no-ops and would take the atomic chart group down. phases[0].why was rewritten in the same proposal as the phases[0].side flip because the old why described Xerath winning level 1. Riot's description of Satchel Charge is magic damage plus a knock-away with no percent-health component, so the flag misfired; Ziggs is entirely magic damage and MR is the correct answer against him. I wrote no edit asserting the opposite. tradeBad still says 'the dash you bought it for' and is quoted verbatim in breakdown.trading and report[3]; not fixable in one place without the three copies disagreeing.
